text:
anna-w: Ran a quick nsys capture on the model loop, timeline looks weird — memcpy bars overlap but GPU kernels are mostly serialized and there are big idle gaps.
mike-l: can you paste the timeline screenshot or the qdrep output? curious about the stream IDs for memcpy vs kernel.
anna-w: attaching the short text export I made from nsys (trimmed):

```
nsys timeline summary:
- stream 3: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (pinned) 0-2.1ms
- stream 3: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 2.5-4.6ms
- stream 1: cuLaunchKernel conv_fwd 0.2-0.9ms
- stream 1: cuLaunchKernel conv_fwd 3.0-3.7ms
- host thread: dispatch gap 0.9-2.5ms (sched sleep)
- stream 0 (default): some cuBlas xGEMM 4.8-5.5ms
```

anna-w: note memcpy bars look concurrent (overlap) but kernels don't run in parallel — they are spaced out by that host dispatch gap.
nsys-bot: reminder: if memcpy uses pageable memory, cudaMemcpyAsync will block the stream until the transfer completes. Use pinned memory for true overlap. :robot_face:
sri-k: do we use pinned buffers? I thought our I/O path writes tensors into a numpy buffer then we call .to(device) which may be causing pageable->pinned implicit copies.
mike-l: that pattern can cause the host thread to block on the copy call, creating the dispatch gap you're seeing. Also check if we accidentally use the default stream: operations in default stream can serialize with memcpy on some drivers.
anna-w: good point — code snippet from our data loader: `buf = np.empty((batch, seq), dtype=np.int64); ... torch.frombuffer(buf).to(device, non_blocking=True)` — we're relying on non_blocking + pinned memory hints but not ensuring pin_memory=True in DataLoader.
sri-k: so two issues: 1) pageable memory -> cudaMemcpyAsync falls back to synchronous staged copies, 2) default stream or user streams ordering semantics. Both can explain serialized kernels.
mike-l: couple of quick checks: 1) verify buffers are pinned (DataLoader pin_memory=True) or use torch.empty(..., pin_memory=True) 2) run nsys with `--trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=nvtx` and add NVTX markers around dispatch to see host events 3) enable `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` only for debugging.
anna-w: I re-ran with pin_memory=True and also added explicit streams for copies + `cudaMemcpyAsync` via torch.to(non_blocking=True). New timeline shows memcpy bars that fully overlap with kernels and the host dispatch gaps shrink.
anna-w: small timeline excerpt after changes:

```
- stream 4: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 0.0-1.9ms
- stream 1: cuLaunchKernel conv_fwd 0.2-0.9ms (overlap with stream4)
- stream 6: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 0.3-2.0ms
- stream 1: cuLaunchKernel conv_fwd 1.0-1.7ms (overlaps too)
- host thread: minimal syscalls, no dispatch gap >50us
```
mike-l: nice! that confirms pinned memory was the primary culprit. Another small thing: on Ampere/GA100 cards you have two copy engines; check `nvidia-smi topo -m` and driver docs. If your copy pattern serializes because you're using the default stream with implicit synchronization, you won't get multi-engine overlap.
sri-k: also saw a case where Python's garbage collector pause caused a 5ms dispatch gap — worth adding tracemalloc/nvtx around allocations in hot path.
anna-w: true — I saw one outlier where an allocation triggered and CPU thread did a syscall. I instrumented with `import gc; gc.disable()` in the hot loop for testing; that removed a few spikes.
mike-l: final action items: 1) enforce DataLoader(pin_memory=True) and ensure tensors created on pinned buffers, 2) annotate code with NVTX markers and capture with nsys `--capture-range=nvtx`, 3) separate copy and compute streams and avoid default-stream implicit sync, 4) add lightweight GC tuning in perf-sensitive loops, 5) add CI perf test to catch regressions.
anna-w: I'll open a PR with DataLoader changes + NVTX markers. uploading short capture to the perf artifacts. cc @sri-k for the GC note.
sri-k: lgtm. if we get another regression, collect a full qdrep and I'll run deeper analysis (perfetto + cpu scheduling sampling). :thumbsup:
mike-l: thanks for the quick triage, anna. this matches the kernel-selection/batching issue we saw earlier where kernels looked like they were mis-selected but were just waiting on host dispatch.\n
